units.title: Catalogue: new entries this week
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: Three additions to the recordings catalogue this week. The headline is Ned's 1976 reservoir dam works reel, digitised from quarter-inch at 7.5 ips, now catalogued with his notes on the tape's condition. Also a 1988 dawn chorus from the Brackwater car park and a Gilliver foghorn from 1971 of uncertain provenance. Metadata corrections welcome. Please do not message me asking whether the reservoir knocks 'match' anything. The catalogue describes; it does not decide.

units.title: The 1976 reservoir tape: about the 'echo'
units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: Good afternoon. Several of you have written to say that each knock on my 1976 dam works tape is preceded by a faint copy of itself, about two seconds early, and that this must be an echo or an answer. It is neither, I am afraid. It is print-through: on a reel stored for decades, the magnetic signal on one layer of tape transfers faintly onto the layer wound against it. Loud sounds leave a ghost on the neighbouring turn. Regards, Ned

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Ned is right and it's worth people learning this one. At 7.5 ips on a standard reel the spacing between adjacent turns works out to a second or two depending on where in the reel you are, so the pre-echo interval drifts slightly through the tape. A real acoustic echo wouldn't drift like that. Quick check for anyone curious: the pre-echo gets longer toward the outside of the reel.

units.title: Quayside after the rain (binaural, 18 min)
units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Headphones on for this one. Weyhaven Quayside, walking west from the swing bridge after the drizzle stopped. Wet tyres hissing left to right, a container crane on the far side doing its long whine above and ahead, gulls on the warehouse roofs behind me, and a lovely moment at 11:20 where a drain gurgles directly under your right foot. Nothing mysterious, just a city breathing out after rain.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Lovely recording. The crane whine is a good example of why I keep saying compressors and motors are everywhere: listen from about 6:00, there's a steady 100 Hz component under the whine that's the mains-frequency hum of the drive, and it carries for hundreds of metres over water. Once you hear that in the city you hear it in every stairwell.

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Good file. The thumping at 14:40 left of centre is a bilge pump on one of the barges by the old dock. Cycles about every forty seconds. That's a pump.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Marlo, you and your pumps. You're probably right, I did walk past a barge with water spilling out of its side. I like that you can name every mechanical noise on a quay from your sofa in Gilliver. Hollis, yes, I hear the hum now and I can't unhear it, thanks so much.

units.title: Cheap recorder clocks: does anyone actually sync them?
units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so slightly awkward question. my school recorder (the cheap one, not the nice one) sets its clock from whatever i type in, and i set it by my phone, which i always assumed was accurate enough. but hollis keeps asking about clock drift on the answering knocks and i realised i've never checked it against anything. how do people sync two recorders 300 m apart? asking for a friend (the friend is me)

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so that is really cool and also slightly disappointing, i had a spectrogram with arrows ready showing the 'pre-knocks' lining up with the brackwater ones. ned, does print-through only go one way? like could there be a ghost after the knock as well as before?

units.title: Brackwater Woods livestream soon
units.author: nightscream_vlog
units.text: guys this is happening. i've been reading the knock threads and i'm going to stream live from brackwater woods, proper night investigation, thermal camera borrowed off a mate, full sound. the knocks are insane and i want you lot to hear them in real time not in some old file. date coming soon, link in bio, share it everywhere

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Good that you're asking. Typed-in clocks on budget recorders commonly drift several seconds a day and can be off by a whole minute if you set them while the phone was still updating. Two cheap fixes: a GPS time logger next to each recorder, or a loud reference sound both units can hear at the start, like an air horn. Then line up on the reference, not the timestamp.

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: A reminder about how this forum works. LowBand is for recordings, not stories, and not for promotion. If you record in Brackwater, post the raw file here with the kit and settings. Please don't send people into private woodland at night; the estate has asked us before. 'Share it everywhere' is not a thing we do on LowBand.

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Pinning this reply for later: if two files are going to be compared by time, the method of synchronisation has to be stated in the post. Tern, there's no shame in this. Most of the regulars learned it by getting it wrong once.

units.author: nightscream_vlog
units.text: with respect ned 'print through' sounds like what someone says when they don't want to admit the reservoir has been doing this since the 70s. the knocks are older than the tape guys. that's the story

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Thanks for posting this, Ned. Print-through is a nice clean explanation for the pre-echoes and I'd be glad to see it put to rest. What it doesn't touch is the main knocks themselves, which are on the tape whether or not there's a ghost of them a turn earlier. I'd still guess dam machinery for 1976. Different question from mine. Make of it what you will.

units.title: Brackwater knocks: week two notes
units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Last night, usual spot on the east path, two omnis at 1.5 m, handheld as backup, gain 42 dB, wind under 2 m/s. Three sets of knocks: 23:58, 00:17 and 00:31, each four to six strikes, evenly spaced, sharp attack, no reverb tail to speak of. Owl pair active throughout. No deer heard. Files uploaded to the shared folder unedited. Make of it what you will.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Hollis's air horn is the right idea but it scares the owls and the gamekeeper both. What I do: GPS logger in the bag, and a hand clap at the start and end that I log by voice. Tern, if you want, we'll do a clap test from both spots next session. No harm done either way.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so i wasn't out last night (marking), but i'll be out at the pumping house spot next time and i'll do the clap thing. dunlin your 00:17 set has a weird double strike at the start, did you see it? might just be wood splitting, i'm not drawing arrows on it yet. i've learned

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: yes please to the clap test. i'm going to check the school recorder's clock against the GPS time on my phone tomorrow in the music room and post what i find, even if it's embarrassing. especially if it's embarrassing, apparently that's the rule

units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: Thank you for cataloguing the reel so carefully. One small correction for the record: the dam works tape was recorded by my late friend Arthur, not by me, on his own machine; I only digitised it. He worked for the water board and recorded the pile driver because he liked the rhythm. I believe it was machinery and I believe he did too. Regards, Ned

units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: Young man, a very good question. Print-through goes both ways. A loud sound transfers to the layer outside it and to the layer inside it, so you can hear a faint ghost before the knock and another after. On most reels the pre-echo is louder than the post-echo because of how the tape is wound, tails out or heads out. On Arthur's reel both are present if you listen. Regards, Ned

units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: Corrected, thank you. Recordist now reads 'A. Treloar (water board)', digitised by N. Ashby. Arthur's notes about the pile driver are added in the description field. I have left 'percussive events, unattributed' on the later sections of the reel, where the pile driver isn't running according to the works log, because I can't attribute them. That's a cataloguing note, not a claim.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Ned, this is such a lovely thread. I listened to Arthur's reel on headphones and you're right, there's a tiny ghost after each knock as well, much quieter, almost like it's coming from inside the tape rather than from the room. Which I suppose it is. I've never thought of a reel as having a memory that leaks.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: Your 'no deer heard' means you didn't hear them, not that they weren't there. There's a group of eight hinds and two stags that use the east path at night. Antlers on a tree, on a gate, on each other. That's your knock. Also the east path is closed after dusk and I'd thank you to keep to it in daylight.

units.title: Gilliver harbour, slack water, 40 min (two hydrophones)
units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Two home-made hydrophones off the harbour wall, one at 2 m, one at 6 m, 40 minutes either side of slack water this evening. Contents: halyards slapping on masts above water, hull slap, the chandlery's pump at 3:10 and every six minutes after, a ferry prop at 22:00 that you feel more than hear, shrimp crackle. No knocks. If you want to know what a harbour sounds like when nothing is happening, this is it.

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Listened to the 00:31 set. Evenly spaced, sharp attack, no tail, repeating. If there's a pump anywhere near that path I'd bet on it. The reservoir outflow has a booster pump, doesn't it? Those can knock on start-up when there's air in the line.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Marlo's pump and my water hammer are the same family. When a valve on the outflow pipe closes quickly, a pressure wave bangs along the pipe, sometimes several times as it settles. Four to six strikes, evenly spaced, sharp attack, little tail: that's textbook. The outflow pipe runs under the east path, if the estate map is right. Has anyone asked the water company about valve schedules?

units.author: tern_audio

edit.note: edited: corrected timestamps after re-checking the drift
edit.text: ok so checked the school recorder against GPS time in the music room. hollis was right. recorder B is 61 seconds fast, not a few seconds, a whole minute. so my 'answering knocks' at 02:41:12 on the day-8 file actually happened at 02:40:11, which means they line up with dunlin's 02:40 set, not his 02:41 set. they're still after his, but 2.1 s after, not 1.5. still answering? i honestly don't know any more. sorry everyone. arrows withdrawn.

units.text: ok so checked the school recorder against GPS time in the music room. hollis was right. recorder B is about a minute out. so my 'answering knocks' at 02:41:12 on the day-8 file need moving, i'm working out which way and by how much, give me a bit. still a beat and a half behind dunlin's though i think. sorry everyone.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Mr Ashcombe, fair point about what I didn't hear, and I'll keep to the path in daylight from now on where I can. I'd only say that antler clash in my old deer files has a wooden, irregular rattle, and these are single strikes at a steady interval. Hollis, the water hammer idea is worth checking. I've written to the water company about valve times.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Thanks for checking and posting it. One line from me: good on you. And note what the correction does and doesn't do. It moves your set onto a different one of dunlin's, at a slightly longer lag. Two sets that both happen to fall a couple of seconds after his is still worth a look. It just isn't a beat and a half any more, and it never was synced.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: No apology needed, tern. A minute out is very normal on that model, I've had worse. Corrected, your set falls just after my 02:40, which is still a curious place for it to fall. We'll do the clap test properly next time and see if anything sits a couple of seconds behind with both clocks right. No theory, just the files.

units.title: Cross-post: footfall count on a stairwell phone recording
units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Cross-posted from the Dellow Court board for audio people, with the raw file owner's permission. Phone recording, mono, 2 min 51 s, single walker descending two flights of 19 treads. Expected events: 38. Counted: 43. The five extras have inter-onset intervals of 0.46 to 0.55 s, matching the walker's own pace. I would welcome a technical second count, not a story.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: I am the walker. Phone in right hand, ordinary trainers, no bag. My phone is old, maybe the microphone is bad, ok. But bad microphone does not add steps with the same speed as me. Please count, then tell me.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: I counted on headphones and got 43 as well, though I'd mark two of the five as uncertain. And I'll say again what I said last week: the extras sit above and behind the mic in a way the walker's own steps don't. Mono or not, the spectrum is different, duller, like they're coming down through concrete from the flight above.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Odile, you cannot localise above and behind from a mono phone file, and in a concrete stair core even binaural cues collapse because reflections arrive from every surface within a few milliseconds. 'Duller' is what you'd expect from structure-borne sound, I agree. It tells you the path, not the direction. That's the bit I'd hold on to.

units.author: nightscream_vlog
units.text: this is literally the scariest file on the site and you lot are arguing about milliseconds. i'm doing the stairwell after brackwater, full stream, 2am, lights off. anyone in dellow want to let me in the front door dm me

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Nobody in Dellow Court will be letting a stranger in at 2am to film the stairwell. Residents live there, including children and elderly people. If you have a technical point about the file, make it. Otherwise this cross-post was a mistake on my part and I would ask the moderator to keep it on topic.

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: This is exactly the kind of file the catalogue needs and nobody ever posts: a baseline. Marlo, would you be willing to add kit details (hydrophone element, preamp, cable length) so lowband_archivist can file it properly? Also, the shrimp crackle at the start is wonderful.

units.author: nightscream_vlog
units.text: i've heard these knocks myself btw, went up there sunday night, they were so loud guys, like someone hitting a tree with a bat right next to you. didn't record it because my phone was on 2 percent but trust me they're real

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Lovely baseline, Marlo. The prop at 22:00 is something else: you can hear the pitch drop as it comes round the breakwater. I'd like to try something similar at the reservoir edge one night, a nothing-happening reference. It would make my knock files easier to read.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so with respect, if they were as loud as a bat on a tree next to you, my recorder would have had them from the pumping house, and on sunday it had nothing but owls and a car on the reservoir road. not saying you weren't there. just saying the files don't agree

units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: I quite understand the appeal of an older mystery. But think of the tape as a roll of wallpaper that was left damp for forty years: where the pattern was heaviest, it has printed faintly onto the roll beside it. Nobody would say the wallpaper was answering itself. The knocks on Arthur's reel are what they are. The ghosts beside them are only the tape remembering. Regards, Ned

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Hollis, I take the point about mono and I'll stop saying 'behind'. But I record stairwells for a living, nearly, and 'duller and coming through the structure from above' is the thing I'd stake something on. Your own explanation agrees with that. So where's the second walker, if there's nobody on the flight above?

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Somewhere else in the building, most likely. Structure-borne footfall can travel several floors in a reinforced frame, and Dellow has two stair cores. Someone on the other core keeping a similar pace for a few seconds is not a stretch. It's not satisfying, I know. It's still more likely than a second walker nobody saw.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: Ok, the other stair core. I live in Dellow nine years, I know the building. The other core is the far end, by the laundry. It is locked at night since two years, with a key only for the caretaker. So who is walking there at 2am with my speed?

units.author: nightscream_vlog
units.text: exactly benedikt, nobody. hollis just makes up a second staircase every time he's losing. this is why nobody takes this forum seriously. at least on my stream people will see it for themselves

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Please don't speak for me. Hollis and I disagree about localisation, we don't disagree about whether he's arguing in good faith. He is. And there's no stream happening in Dellow Court, there are kids who live there and are already scared of those stairs.

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Locking this one. The technical second count has been done (43, with two marked uncertain), the localisation argument has been made on both sides, and the rest has drifted into streams, staircases and who takes whom seriously. Dellow residents have their own board for the building side of it. Thank you to Tobin and Benedikt for posting the file properly.

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Asked around. My cousin's on the water company's maintenance crew. The outflow booster at Brackwater runs on a timer for top-up at night when power's cheap, starts and stops through the small hours. He couldn't tell me the exact times. If dunlin gets the valve schedule I'd put a pint on the knocks lining up with it.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: Pipes, pumps, deer. Take your pick, any of them beats tramping about the woods at midnight with a dish. Rut's tailing off, I'll grant you, so the stags are quieter than they were. But there's nothing in those woods that needs recording at night, and the weekend's going to blow a gale. Stay home.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: No session this weekend, Mr Ashcombe gets his wish, mostly because of the forecast. Wind over 10 m/s makes the omnis useless and the dish a sail. I'll use the time to go through the valve schedule if the water company replies, and to line up last week's files against tern's corrected clock. Make of it what you will.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so i'm actually relieved, i had a parents' evening and a broken keyboard to deal with anyway. i've ordered a GPS logger (£19, it's tiny). when it comes my clock will never be a minute out again and hollis will have to find something else to be right about

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so the wallpaper thing finally made it click for me, thanks ned. i went back and checked and the gap between pre-echo and knock gets longer towards the end of the digitised file, like hollis said. so it's the reel, not the reservoir. that's one mystery down, which honestly feels good this week

units.author: nightscream_vlog
units.text: update guys, the brackwater stream is friday night, weather permitting, which it will. borrowed a second camera. you'll hear everything live, no edits, no 'print through' excuses. if the gamekeeper turns up that's content as well. link in bio

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Second reminder, and the last one before it becomes a warning: no promotion of streams here, and no encouraging people into the estate at night. The Met Office has a gale coming in for the weekend anyway. If you do record something, the raw file goes here, with kit and settings, like everyone else's.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: For anyone who finds this thread later, my full method: GPS logger in the bag, set to one fix per second; hand clap at start and end, called out by voice with the logger time; recorder clock set from the logger on the day; and a note of all of it in the post. It is dull and it works. Tern's correction is in the edit history above for the record.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: printing this out for the music room wall. also going to make the year 9s do it with the cheap recorders as a lesson, because nothing teaches you clock drift like being wrong on the internet in front of everyone

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Kit, for the archive: piezo disc elements potted in resin, home-made preamp on a 9 V battery, 15 m of screened cable, handheld recorder at 48 kHz. Bram ran me out past the wall on his boat for the 6 m drop. The pump at 3:10 is the chandlery's. Rook confirmed it by switching it off for me, which is the most cooperation I've ever had from him.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Marlo, the idea of Rook switching off his pump on request is the most heartwarming thing I've read on here. Listened to the 6 m file on headphones and it's genuinely disorienting, everything is everywhere at once. Water doesn't do left and right, does it.

units.title: Catalogue request: Brackwater recordings, 1980s and 1990s
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: The catalogue has a gap between Arthur's 1976 reel and the first digital files in 2004. If anyone holds cassettes or DAT tapes recorded at Brackwater in those years, birds, weather, anything, I'd like to hear from you. I can arrange digitising through Ned. Provenance matters more than content: who, where, when, what machine.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: My uncle had a cassette walkman he used for the dawn chorus at the reservoir in the early 90s. I'll ask whether the tapes survived the loft. He labelled everything in pencil, so the provenance might actually be good, if faded.
